subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: The demo's Talk renders the kit's Presentation with the presentation-owned steps and title. The shared StoryScene renders the kit's SceneLayer, Box and Frame nodes. Box supplies the kit's layout and layoutId mechanism. StoryScene reuses the kit's EASE, LAYOUT_T, ENTER_T and ENTER_DELAY constants rather than redefining them. The steps are typed with the kit's Step and SceneProps types. Nothing in the demo reimplements the stage, navigation or chrome.
evidence: Talk.tsx: <Presentation steps={STEPS} title={title} initialMode="browse" /> imported from '../../presentation-kit'.
Scene.tsx: StoryScene({ payload }: SceneProps<Beat>) returns <SceneLayer> and renders Box, or Frame for the reveal entity, with id={e.id}.
primitives.tsx Box: <motion.div layout layoutId={id} ...>. Frame, Label, Arrow, Emphasis and SymbolChip all delegate to Box.
Step modules 01–09 are each typed Step<Beat> and set Scene: StoryScene and groupKey: 'story'.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: all nine step modules set groupKey 'story' and Scene StoryScene. Stage compares Scene and groupKey with its stored identity, and for grouped steps it does not compare step id, so the serial stays the same. The motion.div is keyed by that serial, so the same scene instance is kept and receives the new payload. Entity identity is separate. entities.ts gives each entity an id of the form `how-to:${name}`. StoryScene passes e.id as the id prop and as the React key. Box forwards it as layoutId inside Stage's LayoutGroup. Entities that exist in consecutive beats therefore keep the same identity and animate through layout. Every one of the 19 ENTITY ids is consumed by the rendered Node through entitiesAt(beat).map. That includes the connector kinds morph, socket-link and verify-link.
evidence: Step modules 01–09 each declare groupKey: 'story', Scene: StoryScene and payload { beat: N }.
Stage.tsx: setIdentity runs only when Scene or groupKey changes, or when there is no groupKey and the id changes. Otherwise the AnimatePresence child key={identity.serial} is unchanged.
entities.ts: entity() builds id `how-to:${name}`, and entitiesAt(beat) filters on born <= beat, so earlier ids persist in later beats.
Scene.tsx: <Node key={e.id} id={e.id} ...> with Node = Frame or Box.
primitives.tsx Box: layout and layoutId={id}, with id destructured so it is not forwarded to the DOM.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The source is organized with clear boundaries. The registry (presentations/index.ts) lazily loads Talk. Talk only wires the steps, the title and the CSS. Content lives in metadata.ts, geometry and ids in entities.ts, the shared renderer in steps/Scene.tsx, thin per-step modules in steps/NN.tsx, and styling in presentation.css. The required title input is consumed: Talk passes title from metadata.ts to Presentation, which uses it as the main element's aria-label. Every ENTITY, metadata and kit constant I traced is consumed: entities by entitiesAt in StoryScene, EASE, LAYOUT_T, ENTER_T and ENTER_DELAY by Scene.tsx and primitives, MIN_SCALE by useFitScale, and SETTLE_MS by the verification scripts. I found no dead contract.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Every kit node primitive (Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip) renders a motion.div with layout and layoutId={id} and a layout transition. The same id across consecutive steps therefore animates position, size and other layout changes in place. Label and the other node primitives delegate to Box.
evidence: primitives.tsx Box: <motion.div layout layoutId={id} transition={{ layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T, ease: EASE } }} …>.
Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip all render <Box id={id}>.
Stage.tsx wraps the scene in <LayoutGroup>.
The sample's StoryScene keys Box by e.id and passes id={e.id}.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: For ungrouped steps, Stage gives each step a new keyed scene wrapper. It uses AnimatePresence mode="sync", so outgoing and incoming scenes are mounted together. The outgoing wrapper is position:absolute with inset 0, so it is out of layout flow. Both wrappers sit inside one LayoutGroup, so a shared layoutId can animate between them. The kit's Box applies no initial opacity 0 and no delay to layout motion, so nothing hides the incoming copy.

primitives.tsx Box: has no default initial opacity. Its layout transition is { duration: LAYOUT_T } with no delay. The only delayed path is the opt-in Appear.
The scene wrapper's fade-in and fade-out overlap rather than wait, so the entity is not removed before the incoming scene mounts.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: A newcomer's entry delay is ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.45s, which equals the layout duration. The delay applies to entry only (opacity/y, or Appear's own transition), not to layout motion, so continuing entities move immediately. Every registry entity in the sample renders through the delayed path. The one undelayed element, the 'edited ✓' small, has no id, layoutId or registry entry, so it is not an entity under the criterion.
evidence: constants.ts: LAYOUT_T = 0.45; ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T.

Scene.tsx: motion.small data-edited fades in without a delay, but it has no id, layoutId, data-entity or registry entry.

criteria.rationale: The kit provides exit mechanisms: Appear has an exit animation, and Stage wraps scenes in AnimatePresence with a scene exit. subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: fitScale returns a single factor, min((w-left-right)/designW, (h-top-bottom)/designH). Stage applies it as transform: scale(s) to a fixed designW×designH inner box, so the internal composition does not reflow. The stage region uses the same STAGE_LAYOUT insets that the fit subtracts, so the canvas lies inside the area the stage occupies. At 1280×720 browse the scale is min(1232/880, 376/380)≈0.989, giving 870×376 in a 1232×376 region. At 390×844 browse it is min(342/880, 500/380)≈0.389, giving 342×148. Present mode fits likewise. The resize listener updates the scale.
evidence: useFitScale.ts: fitScale uses STAGE_LAYOUT[mode] insets and the min of the two ratios; useFitScale listens to resize.
Stage.tsx: the stage div's inset is built from the same geometry. The canvas is designW*scale by designH*scale, and the inner div has fixed designW×designH with transform: scale(${scale}).
scene.test.tsx 'uniformly fits wide narrow short and resized viewports…' asserts the scaled size does not exceed the area.
judging basis: consensus-pass

scene.test.tsx: expect([DESIGN_W, DESIGN_H]).toEqual([880,380]) and the inner style contains width: 880px and height: 380px.

criteria.rationale: The props are typed as `HTMLMotionProps<'div'>` and `Icon` is destructured off the DOM, which meets the first and third clauses. The identity-hook clause fails: in `Box`, `{...props}` is spread after `layout`, `layoutId={id}`, `data-presentation-node="box"` and `transition`. `NodeProps` includes `layoutId`, so a caller can override the layoutId. `SceneLayer` and `Appear` also spread caller props after `data-presentation-layer` and `data-presentation-appear`. Callers can therefore override the kit's identity hooks.

primitives.tsx SceneLayer: <motion.div data-presentation-layer="" style={...} {...props}>
primitives.tsx Appear: data-presentation-appear="" ... {...props} after it

criteria.rationale: The requirement says browser-driving tests must wait for observable state and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by spawning the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser path sleeps for a fixed time. E2E-001 runs `npm run verify` (tests/integration.test.mjs:125). It then asserts the per-step PASS lines and the title/caption sample validation that verify prints. Inside verify, each step polls `stepIndex` and then calls `page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` (scripts/verify.mjs:39), a fixed 850 ms (scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7). Only after that sleep does it read the title and caption it reports on. INT-002 runs inspect with `--settle 150` (tests/integration.test.mjs:96). Inspect sleeps with `page.waitForTimeout(settle)` (scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:26) before collecting diagnostics and screenshots. The test then asserts on that fixed interval (`step.captured - step.arrived >= 150`, line 102) instead of on a settled signal. So the 'use no fixed sleeps' clause is not met. Judges A and B argued pass because the tests contain no `waitForTimeout` and the scripts poll `data-step-index`. The cited material shows that index polling sits next to the fixed sleeps and does not replace them. The browser the tests drive still waits a fixed number of milliseconds for the transition before the content assertions run. The tests not calling Playwright directly does not remove those sleeps from the browser tests. Their point that the 10 ms `setTimeout` in contracts.test.tsx is a jsdom act flush, not a browser test, is correct, but that is not the basis of this fail.

criteria.rationale: Every test that starts a preview or browser runs the scripts, and `freePort()` in browser-tools.mjs allocates a dynamic port by listening on port 0. No fixed port is shared. The scripts own the Vite process directly and always close it. integration.test.mjs `assertStopped` then checks that the Chromium and preview PIDs no longer exist (`process.kill(pid, 0)` throws ESRCH) and that the preview URL is unreachable. This is checked on success, on every injected-failure case (E2E-002) and in the INT-002 inspect run, so no preview is left behind. The 100s watchdog only kills npm, but it is a timeout fallback, and the scripts' SIGTERM handlers close the preview.

criteria.rationale: Runtime scenarios were well exercised in a browser: step order, present/browse modes, navigation, active state, boundaries, swipe, attribution and fit scaling. A bootstrap copy was also built and verified, and one console-error fault was injected. Several omissions were the candidate's choice, not environmental. The log says it chose not to inject a build fault, a missing or malformed sample, or a stalled transition, which covers 'Build must succeed' failure, 'Missing sample fails' and 'Step error fails'. It also did not exercise any of the Visual inspection artifact warning scenarios: suspicious overlap, intentional overlap, indistinct active chrome and unpolished attribution. The log states they were 'not injected into a controlled variant' and 'remain unverified by acceptance'. The skill-journey scenarios (requirement-002) were disclosed as unexercised because no requestor was available. That is plausibly environmental. The scaffold-fixture scenarios (monorepo, partial scaffold, preservation) could have been tried against scratch fixtures, but the log argues they need the skill agent. The motion scenarios were checked only by settled screenshots, which is weaker than the morph and entry-sequencing scenarios state. The log admits this. Together, the self-chosen omissions in requirement-003 and the motion scenarios leave a substantial share of behavior unexercised.

votes.rationale: Grouping: all nine step modules set groupKey 'story' and Scene StoryScene. Stage compares Scene and groupKey with its stored identity, and for grouped steps it does not compare step id, so the serial stays the same. The motion.div is keyed by that serial, so the same scene instance is kept and receives the new payload. Entity identity is separate. entities.ts gives each entity an id of the form `how-to:${name}`. StoryScene passes e.id as the id prop and as the React key. Box forwards it as layoutId inside Stage's LayoutGroup. Entities that exist in consecutive beats therefore keep the same identity and animate through layout. Every one of the 19 ENTITY ids is consumed by the rendered Node through entitiesAt(beat).map. That includes the connector kinds morph, socket-link and verify-link.
evidence: Step modules 01–09 each declare groupKey: 'story', Scene: StoryScene and payload { beat: N }.
Stage.tsx: setIdentity runs only when Scene or groupKey changes, or when there is no groupKey and the id changes. Otherwise the AnimatePresence child key={identity.serial} is unchanged.
entities.ts: entity() builds id `how-to:${name}`, and entitiesAt(beat) filters on born <= beat, so earlier ids persist in later beats.

The same entity id in consecutive beats therefore morphs in place through Motion's layout mechanism. Every entity in the array is rendered once its `born` beat is reached, so none is dead.

votes.rationale: fitScale returns a single factor, min((w-left-right)/designW, (h-top-bottom)/designH). Stage applies it as transform: scale(s) to a fixed designW×designH inner box, so the internal composition does not reflow. The stage region uses the same STAGE_LAYOUT insets that the fit subtracts, so the canvas lies inside the area the stage occupies. audit_results.rationale: The criterion requires browser-driving tests to wait on observable state and use no fixed sleeps. The guidance fails any test that waits a fixed number of milliseconds for a transition before asserting the step. The quoted lines show the browser test path doing exactly that. E2E-001 runs `npm run verify` and asserts on the per-step PASS output (tests/integration.test.mjs:125-128). verify.mjs drives the browser and asserts on it. At each step it polls stepIndex, then calls `page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` (scripts/verify.mjs:39), a fixed 850 ms (scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7). Only then does it read the title and caption it validates. The index poll comes before the fixed sleep but does not replace it, so the 'no fixed sleeps' clause is unmet. INT-002 likewise drives inspect, which sleeps a fixed `settle` after reaching the step and before collecting diagnostics (scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:24-29). The test then asserts on that fixed interval (line 102) rather than on a settled signal. Not calling waitForTimeout in the test file does not remove these sleeps from the browser tests it runs. The quoted spans are enough to show the unmet clause.

result.rationale: The requirement says browser-driving tests must wait for observable state and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by spawning the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser path sleeps for a fixed time. E2E-001 runs `npm run verify` (tests/integration.test.mjs:125). It then asserts the per-step PASS lines and the title/caption sample validation that verify prints. Inside verify, each step polls `stepIndex` and then calls `page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` (scripts/verify.mjs:39), a fixed 850 ms (scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7). Only after that sleep does it read the title and caption it reports on. INT-002 runs inspect with `--settle 150` (tests/integration.test.mjs:96). Inspect sleeps with `page.waitForTimeout(settle)` (scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:26) before collecting diagnostics and screenshots. The test then asserts on that fixed interval (`step.captured - step.arrived >= 150`, line 102) instead of on a settled signal. So the 'use no fixed sleeps' clause is not met. Judges A and B argued pass because the tests contain no `waitForTimeout` and the scripts poll `data-step-index`. The cited material shows that index polling sits next to the fixed sleeps and does not replace them. The browser the tests drive still waits a fixed number of milliseconds for the transition before the content assertions run. The tests not calling Playwright directly does not remove those sleeps from the browser tests. Their point that the 10 ms `setTimeout` in contracts.test.tsx is a jsdom act flush, not a browser test, is correct, but that is not the basis of this fail.
